## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Running Code

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(palmerpenguins)
install.packages("palmerpenguins")
library(ggplot2)
library(ggthemes)
install.packages("ggthemes")

```

# 

variable = something that is quantity, quality or measurable

observation = measurment made under similar conditions

Value = is the state of variable when you measure it

Tabular data = is a set of valies each associated with a variable and an observation

```{r}
#| echo: true
head(penguins)
# or you can just use glimpse()
glimpse(penguins)


```

\

```{r}
#| echo: true
ggplot(data = penguins,
       mapping = aes(x = flipper_length_mm, y = body_mass_g, color = species)) +
  geom_point() + # this line is a function of which and how to display your data --alternative is geom_bar, geom_line, etc 

  geom_smooth(method = "lm") # lm is linear model 

# after each + new line adds that adds complexity 
# the bare minimum for this is ggplot with mapping aes, and geom_point() which includes all the points together 
# the geom_smooth adds smoothing line per data cluster 
# this can change to one smooth lne or multiple per request on geom_point( inside here specify) 
# see example below - same code - modified inside geom_point(----)

ggplot(data = penguins,
       mapping = aes(x = flipper_length_mm, y = body_mass_g)) +
  geom_point(mapping = aes(color = species, shape = species)) + 

  geom_smooth(method = "lm") # lm is linear model 


# now title naming and all --- how to do 
# with labs ( title - above, subtitle = below title , x and y have their related place and color )

ggplot(data = penguins,
       mapping = aes(x = flipper_length_mm, y = body_mass_g)) +
  geom_point() + # this line is a function of which and how to display your data --alternative is geom_bar, geom_line, etc 

  geom_smooth(method = "lm") + # lm is linear model 

  labs(
    title = "BMI and flipper length",
    subtitle = "Dimensions for Adelie, Chinstrap, and Gentoo penguins",
    x = "Flipper length(mm)", y = "Body mass(g)",
    color = "Species", shape = "Species"
  ) +
  scale_color_colorblind()

  

```

```{r}
#1.4 visualizing distribution 

ggplot(penguins, aes(x = species)) +
  geom_bar()

ggplot(penguins, aes(x = fct_infreq(species))) + 
  geom_bar()

# 1.42

# wide as f width of bar 
ggplot(penguins, aes(x = body_mass_g)) + 
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 2000)

# reasonable 
ggplot(penguins, aes(x = body_mass_g)) + 
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 200)

# reminds me of spaghetti (uncooked)
ggplot(penguins, aes(x = body_mass_g)) + 
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 20)

# lets do density plot instead of geom_bar 

ggplot(penguins, aes(x = body_mass_g)) + 
  geom_density()


ggplot(penguins, aes(x = body_mass_g, color = species)) + 
  geom_density(linewidth = .5 ) 

ggplot(penguins, aes(x = body_mass_g, color = species)) + 
  geom_density(linewidth = 1.0 ) 

ggplot(penguins, aes(x = body_mass_g, color = species)) + 
  geom_density(linewidth = 10 ) 

# -- you can fill inside the color with alpha -- called opacity i think 

ggplot(penguins, aes(x = body_mass_g, color = species, fill = species)) + 
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5)  



# box plot - ya like box plot ? 
ggplot(penguins, aes(x = species, y = body_mass_g)) + 
  geom_boxplot()

```

```{r}

ggplot(penguins, aes(x = island, fill = species)) +
  geom_bar()

ggplot(penguins, aes(x = island, fill = species)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill")


ggplot(penguins, aes(x = island, fill = species)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill") +
  labs(y = "proportion")




```
